fields.why: The Summary's headline comparative claim is fully vaccinated vs unvaccinated cases (milder infections), a two-group contrast; the three-route Kruskal-Wallis comparison is secondary, so the group > pair tie-break is not reached.

The NNDSS 'Gender identity' variable mixes Male/Female with transgender categories, so it reads as the v5 composite (SOGI plus sex) though the article never says it is composite; SOGI alone is also defensible.
The groupwise entry is the Fisher test across the five gender-identity categories; listing sex beside SOGI follows from reading the variable as composite, and SOGI alone is equally defensible.

brief_issues: The comparison rule says to lead with the Summary headline, but its parenthetical 'when pair and group comparisons coexist, group leads' can be read as overriding it; and the composite-variable rule (V15a) does not say whether a 'gender identity' variable with transgender categories, not stated as composite, also records sex.
